unit.unitOverview:
Hello! My name is Zane. I go to Ehel Academy in Hargeisa. I love water! I like to drink it, splash it, and water the plants. In this unit, you will find out how to save water too.

Do these with a grown-up. You can point, talk, tick, draw and count. There are no marks. Just have fun and do your best!

outcomes.text: 5. Draw a way to save water

explainers.title: 1. Where do we use water?
explainers.body:
We use water every day. Read each one with your grown-up. Tick the box for the ways you use water at home.

Now count your ticks. How many ways do you use water at home? Hold up that many fingers!

explainers.title: 2. Water is precious
explainers.body:
Precious means very special. People, animals and plants all need water to live. Point to each one and say: 'You need water!'

Everything that is alive needs water. That is why water is so precious.
bullets: A child having a cool drink.
A little plant in the sun.

explainers.title: 3. Save or waste?
explainers.body:
Some things save water. Some things waste water. Read each one. Say 'save!' with a thumbs up, or 'waste!' with a thumbs down.

Did you find the ways to save water? Well done! Now point to the best way to save water, and try to do it at home today.
bullets: Turn the tap off while you brush your teeth.
Leave the tap running for a long, long time.
Tell a grown-up about a dripping tap.
Let a tap drip all day.
Use only the water you need.

explainers.title: 4. Count the drips
explainers.body: A dripping tap wastes water, drip by drip. Look at the drips below. Count them out loud, and hold up that many fingers.

explainers.title: 5. Draw a way to save water
explainers.body:
Think of one way you can save water. In the box, draw yourself saving water. You could turn off a tap, catch the rain, or water a plant with old water.

You can add bright colours and a big sun to your picture. Now tell your grown-up about it. Start with: 'I can save water by ...'

explainers.title: Before you go
explainers.body:
You have learned so much about water! Answer these out loud with your grown-up.

Well done! Now turn to the Mini-Project & Reflection sheet to make your water poster or say your water promise.
bullets: What is one way we use water?
What is one way you can save water?

lines: There are five drips! Every drip is good water we could save. Can you find a tap at home and check that it does not drip?

bigIdeas.title: Our water promise
lines: I will turn the tap off when I do not need it.
I will not waste clean water.
I will help to look after our world.

tutorPrompts.title: Ask Your AI Tutor (with a grown-up)
lines: With your grown-up, ask your AI tutor: Why do plants need water?
Then tell the tutor one thing that needs water to live.

tutorPrompts.title: Ask Your AI Tutor (with a grown-up)
lines: With your grown-up, tell your AI tutor about your water poster or your water promise.
Ask it: What is one thing you like about my idea?
Then ask for one more easy way to save water at home.

speakingPrompts.title: Talk about it
lines: When did you use water today?
Who fetches the water in your family?

speakingPrompts.title: Talk about it with your grown-up
lines: What is one way you use water?
What is one way you save water?
Who did you tell about saving water?
How did it feel to help look after our world?
Last of all, finish this out loud, or draw the answer: 'The best way I can save water is ...'
Well done! You know how we use water, you know that water is precious, and you can help to save it. You are a real water helper. Every drop counts!

grownUpGuide.label: For the grown-up
grownUpGuide.intro: This part is written for the parent or teacher sitting with the learner, and is kept in their own words.

sections.title: Before you begin
sections.body:
Hello, and welcome to the last Global Perspectives project of Year 1 at Ehel Academy. This guide is written for you, the grown-up. In Global Perspectives, little children do not learn long lists of facts. Instead, they slowly grow gentle thinking-and-talking skills: looking and noticing, talking and listening, caring about our world, and sharing a small idea. In this project they grow those skills through something every child knows and loves: water.

Your child is only about five or six years old, so this project is led by you. You read everything aloud, point to the pictures, ask the questions, and do the little activities together. There is almost no writing. Children look, point, talk, draw, act and count. A warm voice and a few minutes, a couple of times a week, is all you need.

sections.title: About this project: How can we save water?
sections.body:
Over this short unit, you and your child will find out three big, simple ideas: how we use water every day, why water is precious, and how we can all help to save it. Everything builds towards one happy ending: your child makes a water-saving poster, or says a water promise, to share with the family or the class.

The journey is five very short, picture-led lessons, then the little poster-or-promise project, then a gentle look back. Along the way your child goes on a water walk, meets a thirsty plant, plays a save-or-waste game, and learns easy ways to save water at home. Keep it light and playful. Lots of talking is exactly right.

sections.title: Water where we live
sections.body: Here in the Horn of Africa, we know water well. In the dry season, the jilaal, there is less rain, and families are careful with every drop and share what they have. When the rains come again, everyone is glad. So keep this unit warm and hopeful. For a little child, the message is never that water is scary. The message is that water is precious, and that even a small child can help to look after it.

sections.title: The little skills your child will grow
sections.body:
This project gently grows four Global Perspectives skills. Here they are in plain words:

You will not test these skills or give marks. You simply give your child lots of friendly chances to look, talk and care, and you notice out loud when they do. A warm 'What good noticing, Zane!' teaches more than any worksheet.
items: Looking and noticing - spotting where we use water, and where water is being wasted.
Talking and listening - telling a grown-up or a friend a small idea, and really listening back.
Caring about our world - understanding that people, animals and plants all need water.
Sharing an idea - saying one way we can save water, and making a promise to try it.

sections.title: How this unit works at Ehel Academy
sections.body:
Children this young cannot learn on their own, so this unit is led by you, the teacher or parent. Ehel Academy's model for our youngest learners has three parts that work together:

There is no rush and no fixed timetable. Spread the five lessons over two or three weeks, or more. If your child loves the water walk, do it three times. Curiosity is the goal.
items: You, the grown-up, leading the way. You read aloud, point to the pictures, and do the little activities. Each lesson is short, about 15 to 25 minutes, and can be split into even smaller pieces.
Teacher sessions about twice a week. In these live sessions children sing, play the water games, and share their ideas with other little learners.

A friendly AI tutor, used together with a grown-up. The tutor can read aloud, ask your child one simple question, or tell a short water story. At this age the tutor is always used with you sitting right beside your child, never alone.

sections.title: Meet Zane and his friends
sections.body:
So the lessons feel friendly, we follow a small group of children at Ehel Academy in Hargeisa. Your child can imagine playing right alongside them.

As your child meets each new idea, they will see what Zane and his friends do. Then your child does the very same thing, at home or with the class.
items: Zane loves water. He likes to splash, to water the plants, and to help fill the water container at home. He wants to look after every drop.
Amal is kind and careful. She always remembers to turn the tap off.
Sami is full of questions. He wants to know where all the water goes.
Leila loves to draw. She is going to make a bright water-saving poster.

sections.title: How to run the five little lessons
sections.body: Each lesson has the same simple shape: a short Aim (what it is for), a Talk about part (to get your child looking and talking), and a Do part (the fun activity). Read the Aim to yourself, then enjoy the Talk about and Do parts together. Keep every answer welcome. There are no wrong answers here.

sections.title: Lesson 4.1 - How do we use water?
sections.body:
Aim. Your child notices all the ways we use water every day, and meets the word water.

Talk about. Ask: 'When did you use water today?' Help them remember - a drink, washing hands, brushing teeth, cooking, washing clothes. Then ask: 'Where does our water come from at home?' Many families fetch water and keep it in a container or a jerrycan. Talk about who fetches the water in your family.

Do. Go on a water walk together. Walk around your home, or the school, and point to every place where we use water: the tap, the kitchen, the washing, the plants, the water for the goats or hens. Count how many places you find, and hold up that many fingers. Zane found water in six places. How many can your child find?

sections.title: Lesson 4.2 - Why is water so precious?
sections.body:
Aim. Your child understands that people, animals and plants all need water, and meets the word precious (it means very special and important).

Talk about. Ask: 'What would happen to a little plant with no water at all?' Then: 'What happens to us when we are thirsty?' Keep it gentle and hopeful. Water helps everything grow and stay well.

Do. Play thirsty plant. Your child curls up small like a droopy plant with no water. You 'water' them with a gentle pat, and they slowly grow tall and happy again. Then talk about keeping water clean: we keep our drinking water covered so it stays clean and good to use. Dust and dirty hands stay out, and the clean water is saved for drinking.

sections.title: Lesson 4.3 - How can we save water?
sections.body:
Aim. Your child learns easy ways to save water, and meets the words save and waste (to waste means to use too much, or let water run away for nothing).

Talk about. Show a dripping tap, or pretend to be one: 'drip ... drip ... drip ...'. Ask: 'Is a dripping tap saving water or wasting it?' Talk about how a tiny drip, all day long, wastes a lot of good water.

Do. Play the save-or-waste game. Say each thing below and let your child call out 'save!' with a thumbs up, or 'waste!' with a thumbs down:

Finish by trying it for real: turn the tap off together while you brush your teeth tonight.
items: Turn the tap off while you brush your teeth. (save)
Leave the tap running while you brush your teeth. (waste)
Tell a grown-up about a dripping tap. (save)
Let a tap drip all day. (waste)
Use only the water you need. (save)

sections.title: Lesson 4.4 - More ways to save water
sections.body:
Aim. Your child finds more happy ways to save and reuse water (to reuse means to use it again for something else).

Talk about. Ask: 'When it rains, where does all the rain go? Could we catch some of it?' Talk about putting out a bucket to catch the rain for the plants.

Do. Look at these clever ways to save and reuse water, and act each one out together:

Ask your child which one they would most like to try at home. That idea can go on their poster later.
items: Catch the rain in a bucket, and give it to the plants.
When you have washed the vegetables, keep that water for the plants too.
Have a quick wash, not a long one.
Fill a cup to rinse, instead of leaving the tap running.

sections.title: Lesson 4.5 - Sharing our water promise
sections.body:
Aim. Your child gets ready to tell other people how to save water, and practises speaking clearly and kindly.

Talk about. Ask: 'Who could we tell about saving water? Grandma? Our neighbours? The class?' Talk about how good it feels to help other people do a kind thing.

Do. Learn the water chant together. Say it, clap it, and add actions - turn off a pretend tap, then cheer:

Now your child is ready for the final project: a water-saving poster, or a water promise, to share. That is all in the Mini-Project & Reflection sheet.
items: Drip, drip, stop! Turn off the tap.
Save the water, clap, clap, clap!
People, plants and animals too -
We can all save water. Yes we do!

sections.title: Key words for this unit
sections.body: These are the words your child will meet in this project. Say them often and warmly. There is no need to test them.

rows: water
The clear liquid we drink, wash with, and cook with. Every living thing needs it.
tap
Where water comes out. We can turn it on and off.
drip
When water falls in tiny drops, like from a tap that is not shut properly.
save
To use only what we need, so we do not lose good water for nothing.
waste
To use too much water, or let it run away for nothing.
precious
Very special and important. Clean water is precious.
clean
Not dirty. We keep our drinking water clean and covered.
reuse
To use water again, like giving washing water to the plants.
dry season
A time with very little rain. We call it the jilaal. We are extra careful with water then.
promise
When you say you will really try to do something, like saving water.
poster
A big picture with a message, to tell other people something.

sections.title: What you will need
sections.body: Nothing special. Gather a few simple things before you start:
items: Paper and crayons or coloured pencils for drawing and for the poster.
A tap, or a water container, for the water walk.
A cup and a bucket, to show catching and saving water.
The Activity Sheet and the Mini-Project & Reflection sheet from this unit.

sections.title: Using the AI tutor together
sections.body:
At this age, the AI tutor is a gentle helper you use side by side with your child, never a babysitter. Sit together, and let the tutor do the things a patient helper does well:

Whenever you see an Ask Your AI Tutor (with a grown-up) box in the sheets, that is your cue to open the tutor together. Keep it short and cheerful, stay in the room, and if the tutor ever suggests something you would rather skip, simply skip it. You are always in charge.
items: Read aloud. Ask it to read a lesson or a list slowly, so your child can follow.
Ask one question. Ask it to ask your child one friendly question, then let your child answer out loud.
Tell a short story. Ask for a one-minute story about water, a plant, or the rain.

sections.title: The final outcome: a water-saving poster or a water promise
sections.body:
Everything leads to this happy ending. Your child chooses their best way to save water, and either draws a water-saving poster or says a water promise out loud, then shares it with the family or the class. The simple, child-friendly steps are in the separate Mini-Project & Reflection sheet.

Your job is to help with the drawing, write down any words your child asks for, and cheer them on. A bright, wobbly poster that your child is proud of is a complete success.

sections.title: Thinking about our work
sections.body:
To finish, help your child look back and feel proud. Keep it gentle and spoken. The Mini-Project & Reflection sheet has happy faces to tick, water drops to colour, and a few talking questions such as:

This looking-back is a real Global Perspectives skill, and it matters as much as the poster. When children hear that their caring and their ideas are valued, they learn the lesson that lasts.
items: What is one way you use water?
Why is water precious?
What is one way you can save water?
Who did you tell about saving water?

sections.title: Keeping it warm and fun
sections.body: You now have everything you need. Go at your child's pace, and sing and splash and talk far more than you worry about getting it 'right'. If your child finishes this unit knowing that water is precious, and that even they can help to save it, then this project has done its job beautifully. Have fun, together.

project.title: Mini-project
project.intro: This is the big one! At Ehel Academy, Zane and his friends made water-saving posters and said their water promises. Now it is your turn. With a grown-up, you are going to make a water-saving poster, or say a water promise, to share with your family or your class. Take your time, and have fun.

steps.title: Choose your best idea
steps.intro:
Think of your best way to save water. Here are some ideas to help you choose:

Say your idea out loud to your grown-up. This is the idea for your poster or your promise. Zane chose to catch the rain for his plants. What will you choose?
items: Turn the tap off while you brush your teeth.
Tell a grown-up about a dripping tap.
Catch the rain in a bucket for the plants.
Give the washing water to the plants.
Have a quick wash, not a long one.

steps.title: Make your poster
steps.intro: Now draw your poster! In the box, draw your water-saving idea. Make it big and bright, so everyone can see it. You can draw yourself in the picture too, saving water with a smile.

steps.title: Add your words
steps.intro:
A poster has a few words too. Ask your grown-up to help you write your idea at the top, in big letters. You could write:

Point to your words, and read them together. Big letters are easy for everyone to read.
items: Save water!
Turn off the tap.
Every drop counts.

steps.title: Say your water promise
steps.intro:
Now stand up tall and say your water promise out loud. A promise is when you really mean to try. Say:

Finish your promise with your best idea. Say it clearly, and with a big smile!
items: I promise to save water. I will ...

steps.title: Share it with everyone
steps.intro:
Show your poster and say your promise to your family or your class. Tell them:

You can finish with the water chant. Say it together, with claps and actions:
items: what your poster shows
one way they can save water too
Drip, drip, stop! Turn off the tap.
Save the water, clap, clap, clap!
People, plants and animals too -
We can all save water. Yes we do!

reflection.prompt: Now the project is finished, it is time to look back and feel proud. Read each line with your grown-up. Tick a happy face if you did it, or a straight face if it is not quite there yet.
How well did you look after water today? Colour in a star for every way you helped. Colour as many as you like!
How do you feel about your water project? Circle one face:

assessment.note: Stages 1-3 are assessed through the mini-project and the look-back grid; the source pack ships no quiz.

selfAssessment.statement: I can name a way we use water.
I know that people, animals and plants all need water.
I can say one way to save water.
I shared my poster or my promise.
